title: Steve Jobs on 10 years of the PC (1991): innovation vs standards, owning core technology
summary: In a 1991 interview as NeXT CEO, Jobs argues that real progress comes from revolutionaries who leap beyond standards, not from incremental evolution. He says the industry is still in its infancy, and that companies must own their underlying technologies and be led by people who understand engineering and manufacturing.

principles.text: Healthy industries need tension between standards and innovation; innovators build on standards, then leap beyond them.
principles.quote: there is a constant tension in our industry between standards and innovation and i think it's a healthy tension

principles.text: Revolution, not evolution, moves an industry forward; revolutionaries must reach critical mass before the incumbents catch up.
principles.quote: it's this tension between the evolution and the revolution that i think keeps our industry moving forward

principles.text: The next big advantage comes from improving group collaboration, not just individual productivity.
principles.quote: improving individual productivity isn't enough anymore the real competitive advantage in the 90s is going to come from improving improving group productivity and collaboration

principles.text: Stay optimistic: every major technological shift reopens the field to new players and new approaches.
principles.quote: we're about one inch down a road that's many miles long and that every time there's major technological innovation there's a tremendous opportunity for new players

principles.text: Take responsibility for your core component technologies instead of outsourcing them and just packaging the result.
principles.quote: we have to have more accountability for our raw technologies and not just assume that we can be the final packager at the end

principles.text: Companies need leaders with engineering and manufacturing backgrounds who understand their dependence on underlying technology.
principles.quote: the management of our companies is not from an engineering or manufacturing background anymore and may not appreciate uh the dependence we have on these underlying technologies
